name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 184 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 22% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 184 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 22 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces in Kashmir have killed the last known local Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist, and Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that no local terrorists remain in the valley. In Manipur, bodies of villagers killed in an October attack were handed over to families after an agreement, while a spurious liquor tragedy prompted security operations and hospitalisations. In Chhattisgarh, forces recovered arms, ammunition and explosives from Maoist dumps in Dantewada and Kondagaon. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Kashmir har drept den siste kjente lokale Lashkar-e-Taiba-terroristen, og unionens innenriksminister Amit Shah kunngjorde at ingen lokale terrorister lenger er i dalen. I Manipur ble likene til landsbyboere som ble drept i et angrep i oktober overlevert til familiene etter en avtale, mens en falsk alkoholtragedie førte til sikkerhetsoperasjoner og sykehusinnleggelser. I Chhattisgarh gjenvant styrker våpen, ammunisjon og sprengstoff fra maoistiske lager i Dantewada og Kondagaon. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
